records.summary: Tasaki Problem 2.1.g / eq. (2.1.34), p. 20: the general-spin closed form of the pi-rotation about axis 3, spinSPiRotation3 N, equals the exponential exp(-i*pi*S^{(3)}) via spinSRot3 N Real.pi. Proved for axis 3 only; the identification for axes 1 and 2, and its many-body lift (Tasaki Problem 2.2.a), remain unformalised, so the coverage of the source item is partial.

Tasaki Problem 2.2.a (b): for alpha and beta distinct, the global pi-rotations U_pi^{(alpha)} and U_pi^{(beta)} anticommute whenever |Lambda|*N is odd, i.e. |Lambda|*S is a half-odd integer. Proved for the closed-form pi-rotation matrices spinSPiRotationAxis and their uniform lattice tensor manyBodySPiRotation; the identification of those closed forms with the book's exp(-i*pi*S^{(alpha)}) at general S is not formalised, so the coverage of the source item is partial.

Tasaki Problem 2.2.a (a): for alpha and beta distinct, the global pi-rotations U_pi^{(alpha)} and U_pi^{(beta)} commute whenever |Lambda|*N is even, i.e. |Lambda|*S is an integer. Proved for the closed-form pi-rotation matrices spinSPiRotationAxis and their uniform lattice tensor manyBodySPiRotation; the identification of those closed forms with the book's exp(-i*pi*S^{(alpha)}) at general S is not formalised, so the coverage of the source item is partial.

Tasaki Problem 2.2.a (c): when |Lambda|*N is odd, every nonzero eigenvector of the global pi-rotation U_pi^{(alpha)} is orthogonal to its image under the anticommuting global pi-rotation U_pi^{(beta)}, alpha and beta distinct. Proved for the closed-form pi-rotation matrices spinSPiRotationAxis and their uniform lattice tensor manyBodySPiRotation; the identification of those closed forms with the book's exp(-i*pi*S^{(alpha)}) at general S is not formalised, so the coverage of the source item is partial.
The Pauli X matrix squares to the identity.

On a connected graph with a real, symmetric, edge-supported, strictly ferromagnetic spin-S coupling, the eigenspace of the Heisenberg Hamiltonian alone at the saturated-ferromagnet energy equals the linear span of the ladder family generated from the all-up state; this is the H-only ground-state eigenspace identity of Tasaki's Theorem 2.1, for a weighted generalisation of the printed uniform coupling.

On a connected graph with a real, symmetric, edge-supported, strictly ferromagnetic spin-S coupling at the printed uniform strength, the Heisenberg Hamiltonian minus its ground energy is positive semidefinite, its ground eigenspace equals the linear span of the ladder family generated from the all-up state, i.e. the states of eq. (2.4.10), and that eigenspace has dimension |V|*N + 1 = 2*S_max + 1. The companion joint-eigenspace result in the same module adds that every ground state has maximal total spin; the printed converse, that these are the only states of maximal total spin, is not proved.

On a connected graph with a real, symmetric, edge-supported, strictly ferromagnetic spin-S coupling, the eigenspace of the Heisenberg Hamiltonian alone at the saturated-ferromagnet energy equals the joint eigenspace of that Hamiltonian and the total-spin Casimir at the saturated values; this is the ground-state half of Tasaki's remark after eq. (2.4.10), that every ferromagnetic ground state carries maximal total spin, and not the converse inclusion the remark also asserts.
